[b]If you have ever wanted to dress up as a giant flamingo, infiltrate a high-society fashion show, and assassinate a corrupt billionaire by kicking him into a grape shredder, Hitman World of Assassination is your dream game. It is less of a traditional shooter and more of a deeply morbid, incredibly beautiful puzzle sandbox where Agent 47, a genetically engineered peak predator, proves his greatest weapon isn't a silenced pistol, but rather a well-timed coin toss, a wet floor sign, or a homing briefcase that defies the laws of physics. The comedic irony is unmatched: 47 is a six-foot-tall, pale, bald man with a giant barcode stamped on the back of his head, yet the moment he puts on a chef's hat, highly trained security guards immediately think, "Ah yes, that's obviously Tobias, he's worked here for five years." Between the clockwork map design that offers fifteen different ways to ruin a target's day and the brutally addictive, rogue-like Freelancer mode, you will easily lose hundreds of hours to this game.

To actually get to this point, however, players had to survive an absolutely unhinged, multi-year corporate journey. Back in 2016, Hitman 1 launched as a controversial episodic experiment, Hitman 2 arrived in 2018, requiring a confusing account-linking ritual to import your old maps, and Hitman 3 launched in 2021 with an absolute Excel spreadsheet of digital licensing "Access Passes" that required a literal PhD to understand. Thankfully, developer IO Interactive finally looked at the chaotic mess they created and consolidated all three games, over 20 massive maps, and hundreds of targets into this single, glorious launcher. It is the gaming equivalent of a band finally putting out a "Greatest Hits" box set after making you buy three different formats of the same album, making it the absolute definitive stealth experience. 10/10, Poisoned a target with spaghetti, hid his bodyguard in a freezer, and escaped on a motorized dolphin.[/b]

Would have loved to get back into this but guess that's not in the cards for me.

This review is solely a critique on the purchase practice. The game is very well made and should be considered by classic hitman fans or anyone who is looking for an immersive stealth sandbox experience. With that said this game is unfortunately spoiled for me by a manipulative and predatory payment structure that has 0 regard to the owners of Hitman 1 and 2. Having around 150 hrs in both games and their DLCs and max progression I would appreciate if I don't have to pay $70 (more with DLCs) to have access to what I have previously owned. This game acts as the central hub and is supposedly THE definitive way to play the 3 games, however, progression cannot be imported as of Feb 2026 and owned DLCs have to be repurchased for another $20-30. This is a non issue had they not delist all the individual games and force the consumer to buy into their confusing payment shenanigans which breaches our trust and loyalty. I adore the franchise and especially this iteration of Hitman but I cannot wholeheartedly recommend this game without doing your research and knowing exactly what you are buying with your money. 

tldr: wait for sale

As good as this series may be, I just cannot get behind the extremely confusing and borderline predatory way that they have gone about presenting the many DLCs, packs, etc. I have no idea what bundle does what. On top of that, IOI wants me to pay again to be able to play a game I already own because they delisted it. No thank you. I regret not getting a refund when it turned out I bought the wrong version of the game.

You have to literally study to understand what each DLC package provides. 

Even better is if you didn't transfer progress and content ownership from Hitman 1 or/and 2 before a certain date, you can't do it anymore. Great way to induce FOMO when Hitman 3 came out.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that virtual reality (VR) features are locked behind higher-priced editions or full-game purchases despite store page labeling.

citations.review_text: Game says its VR supported and then they hide the feature behind a 60$ paywall, ridiculous

This game is being sold under the full title HITMAN World of Assassination, it shows up that way on the store, and the banner even advertises "VR Supported".
In reality, this is HITMAN World of Assassination Part One — basically just the original Hitman 1 missions. It’s missing huge chunks of content (no Freelancer mode, no later episodes), and despite the prominent “VR Supported” banner, the store description later quietly admits it “Does not include VR or Freelancer modes”.
This feels like a deliberate bait-and-switch. The packaging and presentation make it look like the complete definitive edition, when it’s closer to a glorified demo or the bare-bones starting package. New players expecting the full World of Assassination experience are going to be seriously disappointed.
If you already own Hitman 1 or are looking for the complete game with all missions, VR, and Freelancer, skip this version and get the proper bundle or wait for a sale on the full edition. Valve and IO Interactive should clean this up — the store page is highly misleading.

citations.review_text:
I've got a stupid amount of time in this game and I'm still finding new stuff. That's probably the biggest compliment I can give it.

Every map feels alive. You can replay the same mission over and over and it'll still feel fresh. 
One run you're the perfect assassin, the next you're dressed as a mascot throwing a screwdriver at someone's head because your original plan completely fell apart - And Somehow... both work.

The freedom is what makes this game so addictive. There's never just one way to complete a mission. Whether you want Silent Assassin or complete chaos, the game lets you play however you want.

The level design is unreal. Even after countless hours I'm still finding new rooms, conversations and shortcuts. Freelancer is also brilliant, it makes every decision matter, and one dumb mistake can ruin an entire campaign.

The amount of detail that's been put into this game is insane, and the performance on PC is awesome!
It looks amazing, runs smoothly, and every location has its own personality.

Easy 10/10. One of the most repayable games I've ever played, and I still keep coming back for "one more mission" -  which somehow always turns into five.

World of Assassination is less of a traditional stealth game and more of a highly lethal, dark puzzle box. You are dropped into massive living environments and told to eliminate a target. How you do it is entirely up to you. You can play it like a grim spy thriller, or you can lean into the game’s glorious "♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥" energy. Striking a perfect balance between serious infiltration and absurd mechanical comedy, the game allows you to drop a coin, choke a guard, steal a chef’s uniform, and poison a celebrity’s hot pot with a straight face. Visually, the engine holds up beautifully. The crowds are dense, the lighting is cinematic, and wandering through these sprawling locations feels like a high stakes vacation. It is a triumph of mechanical design. It rewards patience, rewards creativity, and offers hundreds of hours of replayability for anyone who loves mastering a space. While the gameplay loop is incredibly addictive, it isn’t flawless. On standard difficulties, guards can feel incredibly oblivious.  But as a pure stealth playground, there is simply nothing else like it on the market. Turn off the hints, put on the signature suit, and start experimenting. It is, without a doubt, the most refined and mechanical version of Hitman ever made.

Hitman is arguably one of the best incarnations of the stealth genre ever created .
While many stealth games rely on scripted events or predetermined paths, Hitman builds true sandboxes where players enjoy a level of freedom that is rarely matched .
The game’s greatest strength lies in its level design. Each map is dense, coherent, and brimming with opportunities . 
Every environment feels like a living, breathing place rather than just a gameplay arena . 
The more you explore a map, the more it reveals new possibilities, making replayability exceptional especially the first map in Paris, which is the most accomplished .
Agent 47 is the perfect protagonist for this game . 
His cold, methodical nature aligns seamlessly with the series’ tone, which oscillates between serious espionage thriller and dark humor . 
Some of the game’s eliminations are deliberately ridiculous, yet they fit surprisingly well into its identity .
The stealth mechanics remain remarkably solid . 
Disguises, restricted area management, observing routines, and exploiting accidents constantly offer fresh approaches . 
The game rewards planning and knowledge of the levels over pure reflexes, giving it lasting depth and high replayability . 
Each map must be played multiple times to be fully appreciated .
That said, the game is not without its flaws . The AI can sometimes be inconsistent, as is often the case in stealth games . 
Some NPC behaviors feel believable, while others can seem artificial . 
The detection system also occasionally produces odd reactions from an aging AI.
The story is likely the least compelling aspect of the experience . 
It serves its purpose as a thread connecting the missions, but nothing more . 
Some challenges also rely more on trial and error or prior knowledge of specific scripts rather than genuine player deduction .
Despite these shortcomings, Hitman is a masterclass in game design . 
Few games offer so much freedom while maintaining such consistenc…

After playing the campaign, I can confidently say Hitman: World of Assassination is one of the best stealth games I've ever played.

Também existem requisitos de conexão online em algumas plataformas, o que incomoda quem prefere jogar totalmente offline.

Fora isso, o jogo se mantém ativamente atualizado, com suporte contínuo da IO Interactive mesmo anos após o lançamento original.

Recomendo bastante, principalmente pra quem gosta de rejogar fases de formas diferentes e não se importa em navegar por um menu de compra um pouco confuso.

Hitman WOA represents what AAA games could be. It reaches across genres that seemingly shouldn't be compatible -- sandbox, action-stealth, puzzle -- and yet this contrast is what makes it entirely unique while also being emblematic of its gameplay. It is both serious and goofy. Guided and freeform. Direct or elaborate. Safe or risky. Every successful mission can end in a perfect, clean getaway or a messy, adrenaline-fueled scramble for the nearest exit. 

The vast majority of missions are large, open-ended levels with one or more targets, sometimes with various optional side objectives. You can explore and complete these missions in whatever way you can devise. Figuring out each level's paths and secrets will test your ability to problem-solve and think outside the box. Every successful mission unlocks more weapons, gear, gadgets, outfits, starting locations, shortcuts, etc., which opens the potential for more playstyles and replayability. Still, even the standard version gives you what is essentially three games in one. It looks great, is well optimized, and there's a ton of content, but the gameplay above all is what elevates it to greatness. The map design, gameplay options, and general vibe of the game are unique and interesting. 9/10, You Should Play It. I enjoyed my time so much I'm actually listing the cons first.

CONS:
- Always online bullenscheisse that doesn't even stop cheaters from populating the leaderboards, not a fan. This is foremost a singleplayer game and I don't appreciate always online ever. 

-  Elusive target time gating in a 6 year old game is very irritating. I do have the signature suit with gloves now but it took a solid three months with no way to speed it up.

- Buying the correct version of this game is surprisingly challenging! Almost feels like a scam sometimes. Luckily I got it right the first time I opened my wallet.

- Freelancer is interesting in concept but difficult to the extreme even for a roguelike. Let us keep some of the weapons or something, it's wild how much you stand to lose per run.

- Game is brutal on the hardware, in a very weird way. PROS:
There isn't really a need to go point by point here I adore most of the g…

Hitman is my most-played game BY FAR. It's sandboxy, puzzle-stealth gameplay that flourishes under creativity has kept me hooked for more than a year at this point. I consistently boot up this expansive game for it's many challenges such as SASO, VR, Freelancer, Elusive targets (limited-time targets), and events. This game has more content in just one map than an entire mobile game at times. The price in this case is DEFINATELY worth the product, with each map containing many escalations, targets, challenges and a whole roguelike looter-shooter mode. The only issues I have with the spectacular game is the confusing ways to purchase the game, and the many useless dlcs (don't buy). Other than that, this game is a MUST-BUY in the stealth genre.

After putting almost 300 hours into this game, I can honestly say it's one of the best stealth games I've ever played. Every location is packed with detail, NPCs actually feel alive, and there are so many different ways to complete each mission that it never gets boring. Even after finishing the campaign, I keep coming back to try new routes, challenges, and Freelancer mode, which I love the most after finishing almost every mission in the game.

The Seven Deadly Sins DLC was also a really fun addition. I liked how each chapter had its own unique theme and gameplay twists instead of just being the same missions again. It was a nice change of pace and gave me another reason to revisit maps I'd already played many times. I also enjoyed the Elusive Target Arcade missions since they add extra challenge with different restrictions and objectives. They make you think more carefully about your approach instead of relying on the same strategies every time, which keeps the game feeling fresh even after hundreds of hours.

Now let's be realistic. I hate how confusing the Deluxe edition and upgrade system is. It shouldn't take research just to figure out what version to buy or what content you're missing. The game itself is amazing, but the way it's sold is unnecessarily complicated. They really could've made the whole process much simpler.

Other than that, I have almost nothing bad to say. Great gameplay, incredible replay value, and probably the best assassination/stealth sandbox ever made. If you're even remotely interested in stealth games, I highly recommend giving it a try.

P.S. Buy Patient Zero & Requiem Pack. You won't regret it.
